questions.question: In UPSC REVISION: Environment & Ecology (Days 85–90), this exam clue belongs to which area: "A.G. Tansley is associated with the concept of ecosystem, meaning organisms and their physical environment functioning together as one system, Ernst Haeckel is..."?
questions.explanation: Ecology Recap: A.G. Tansley is associated with the concept of ecosystem, meaning organisms and their physical environment functioning together as one system, Ernst Haeckel is associated with ecology, the study of interactions between organisms and their environment. Lindeman's 10 percent law says only about one-tenth of energy passes from one trophic level to the next. An ecotone is a transition zone between two ecosystems; edge effect means species diversity is often high at that boundary. A niche is the functional role of a species, including where it lives, what it uses, and how it interacts in the ecosystem. Mutualism is a +/+ interaction where both species benefit; lichen is the standard example of algae and fungus association.

questions.question: In UPSC REVISION: Environment & Ecology (Days 85–90), this exam clue belongs to which area: "India has four biodiversity hotspots: Himalaya, Western Ghats, Indo-Burma, and Sundaland/Nicobar region. In-situ conservation protects species inside their natural..."?
questions.explanation: Biodiversity Recap: India has four biodiversity hotspots: Himalaya, Western Ghats, Indo-Burma, and Sundaland/Nicobar region. In-situ conservation protects species inside their natural habitat, such as National Parks and Biosphere Reserves, whereas Ex-situ conservation protects species outside natural habitat, such as zoos, botanical gardens, gene banks, and seed banks. IUCN Red List categories include Critically Endangered and Endangered; Great Indian Bustard is commonly cited as Critically Endangered and tiger as Endangered.

questions.question: In UPSC REVISION: Environment & Ecology (Days 85–90), this exam clue belongs to which area: "UNFCCC came from the 1992 Rio Earth Summit and is the framework convention for climate change negotiations. Kyoto Protocol set binding greenhouse gas emission reduction..."?
questions.explanation: Treaties Recap: UNFCCC came from the 1992 Rio Earth Summit and is the framework convention for climate change negotiations. Kyoto Protocol set binding greenhouse gas emission reduction targets mainly for developed countries. Paris Agreement uses Nationally Determined Contributions, where countries submit their own climate action targets. Montreal Protocol protects the ozone layer; Kigali Amendment targets phasedown of HFCs. Convention on Biological Diversity is linked with Nagoya Protocol on benefit sharing and Cartagena Protocol on biosafety.

questions.question: In UPSC REVISION: Environment & Ecology (Days 85–90), this exam clue belongs to which area: "Wildlife Protection Act, 1972 protects wild animals, birds, and plants through schedules of protection. Environment Protection Act, 1986 is an umbrella law giving the..."?
questions.explanation: Indian Laws Recap: Wildlife Protection Act, 1972 protects wild animals, birds, and plants through schedules of protection. Environment Protection Act, 1986 is an umbrella law giving the Union government broad powers to protect the environment. National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 created a specialized tribunal for environmental cases. Forest Rights Act, 2006 recognizes forest rights and gives Gram Sabha an important role in claims and community forest resource protection.

questions.question: In UPSC REVISION: Environment & Ecology (Days 85–90), this exam clue belongs to which area: "High Biological Oxygen Demand indicates organic pollution because microbes consume more dissolved oxygen. Eutrophication is nutrient enrichment of water bodies leading..."?
questions.explanation: Species & Pollutants: High Biological Oxygen Demand indicates organic pollution because microbes consume more dissolved oxygen. Eutrophication is nutrient enrichment of water bodies leading to algal bloom and oxygen depletion. Biomagnification is the increase in concentration of persistent toxins at higher trophic levels. Fly ash is a major particulate waste from coal-based thermal power plants.

lesson_intro: Today we wrap up 'Environment & Ecology'. You have mastered the science of ecosystems, the laws of conservation, and the international diplomacy of climate change. For UPSC, Environment is the 'Deciding Factor'—it bridges the gap between geography and current affairs. Today, we consolidate the treaties and the species. Can you remember the 4 Hotspots? The 10% law? The Paris NDCs? Let's master the green marks today.
